medium: Pencil on a spiral-bound sketchbook page
provenance: Drawn by Larry from memory on 2026-09-05, the day of the photograph-by-photograph sitting. His son photographed the page in the sketchbook the same afternoon (phone photograph, file timestamp 13:31) and sent it to the archive; the sheet stays with the family. Whether he was asked to draw or drew unprompted, and what he said while drawing, were not recorded.
title: Base camp, “Ton Son Nhut”
description: A plan of the camp, drawn in pencil on a sketchbook page. A long line runs along the top edge, with ARMORY WALL written along it and, at its left end, a small box with the word OUR inside. In the top-right corner a large box is labelled EM CLUB. Down the left side, below the wall line, are five boxes in three rows: a pair at the top, of which the left-hand box runs off the page edge; a pair below, of which the right-hand box is labelled MY HOOCH and the left-hand box runs off the page edge; and a larger box in the bottom-left corner, open at the page edge. In the lower centre a box labelled SHOWER has short hatching on its left and right sides, a scribbled stroke over the word, a row of short marks after it, and two small figures drawn on its bottom edge, left of centre; a curved line loops around its right side. The words BASE CAMP TON SON NHUT are written diagonally across the middle of the page. Nothing on the sheet indicates scale, compass direction, or which way the camp faced.
researchNotes: The sheet agrees with what he has said at the photographs, in the same words: on 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-05 he put the EM Club 'right across from' and 'about 50 yards from' his hooch (VN-0030 to VN-0034), and described the building beside his hooch as 'our units armory' with the EM Club just off the right edge of that frame (data/recollections/giscus-vn-0082-c18259944.json). The drawing places the armory wall along the top of the camp and the EM Club in the far corner from his hooch, which is a layout, not a distance; the two accounts are consistent but the sheet adds nothing about how far apart they stood. The spelling TON SON NHUT is his own hand, a third rendering after 'Ton Son Nuht' (typed comments, 2026-08-13) and his son's transcriptions; all are recorded on the place record. The camp is not identified from documents; this drawing is his testimony about it, not evidence of where it was.
